title: Natural not as part of man's essence but as created with him, like the body's proportion and beauty
source_text: XXVI. Porro justitiam istam primo homini ante lapsum naturalem fuisse, & dici debere contendunt. Non quidem quod fuerit pars essentiam naturae humanae constituens, aut quod ex humanae naturae principiis necessario fluxerit: sed quia fuit aliquid naturae concreatum, & ad dotes nativas humanae naturae nondum lapsae pertinens. Adeoque justitia illa Originalis, secundum eorum doctrinam, donum naturale fuit, non supernaturale. Et se habet respectu animae hominis integri, quomodo respectu corporis se habebat justa membrorum proportio & pulchritudo, vigor atque decor, quae in eo tum reperiebantur, quaeque naturalem quandam, non vero supernaturalem perfectionem hominis spectabant: licet non essent de essentia hominis, neque etiam ex naturae humanae principiis necessario fluerent.
pass_a_gloss: Further they contend that that justice was natural to the first man before the fall, and ought to be called so. Not indeed because it was a part constituting the essence of human nature, or because it flowed necessarily from the principles of human nature: but because it was something concreated with nature, and pertaining to the native endowments of human nature not yet fallen. And so that Original justice, according to their doctrine, was a natural gift, not supernatural. And it stands in respect of the soul of integral man as the just proportion and beauty of the members, vigor and comeliness, stood in respect of the body, which were then found in him, and which regarded a certain natural, not supernatural perfection of man: although they were not of the essence of man, nor also flowed necessarily from the principles of human nature.
pass_b_english: They further maintain that this righteousness was natural to the first man before the fall and should be called natural. They do not mean that it was a part making up the essence of human nature, or that it flowed necessarily from the principles of human nature. They mean that it was created together with that nature and belonged to the native endowments of human nature before the fall. On their teaching, then, original righteousness was a natural gift, not a supernatural one.

It stood to the soul of unfallen man as the due proportion and beauty of the limbs, their strength and grace, then stood to his body. Those belonged to a natural, not a supernatural, perfection of man, even though they were not part of his essence and did not flow necessarily from the principles of human nature.

choices.why: Concreatum is the key Reformed term: given at creation, not added later; the English spells that out.
